text:
anika: Heads-up: bringing up model 'mistral-compat-v0.9' quantized (q4_0) for multilingual evals — focused on zh/jp/ko + ar/he. Initial runs show CJK tokenization explosion and an RTL reorder regression in en->ar translate. Details below.

liam: @anika can you paste the eval summary?

anika: Sure, quick grep from eval run (multilingual-suite v2):
```
model: mistral-compat-v0.9-q4_0
datasets: wmt21, opensubs, internal-rtl-test
avg_tokens_per_input: en: 124, zh: 322, ja: 289
BLEU (en->zh): 25.3 (-0.4 vs float16)
BLEU (en->ar): 18.1 (-3.7 vs float16)
qscore/chrF: zr drop noted on CJK
```
CJK token count ~2.6x floating baseline, truncation happening.

kenji: Interesting — likely sentencepiece vocab mismatch; q4 quantization shouldn't change tokenizer. Are you using the same tokenizer files?

anika: Yes, same tokenizer.tar in model package. But I noticed many single-char tokens for zh and ja, looks like normalization step skipped (NFKC) so fullwidth punctuation not merged.

maya: @kenji I remember we had a similar issue with a model where the tokenizer config had 'remove_extra_whitespace: true' missing. Could that cause extra splits?

kenji: Maybe. Also check 'use_regex_pretokenize' flag. For Japanese we prefer mecab pretokenize before spm to reduce tokens.

anika: Added quick diff of tokenized sample:
```
input: 我爱ML平台
spm tokens (broken): ▁我 ▁爱 ▁M L 平 台 -> 8 tokens
expected tokens: ▁我爱ML平台 -> 2-3 tokens
```
This inflates token consumption and causes the model to hit max_length.

evals-bot: Automated regression detected: en->ar BLEU drop >= 3.0; alerts: <link to run/1765201234>. Suggested checks: tokenizer cfg, right-to-left postprocessing, BPE merge table integrity.

liam: For RTL, could be postprocessing strip that reverses tokens incorrectly after detokenization. Check 'bidi' handling in generation pipeline.

anika: I ran a diff between float16 and q4 output for one en->ar example. Float16: 'مرحبا بك في المنصة.' Q4: 'لك في المنصة مرحبا.' — word order reversed in many cases.

maya: That's a classic detokenization error where joiner/directional markers are lost. Are we passing U+200F RLM markers in the tokenizer? Or stripping them in postprocess?

anika: I re-ran with 'preserve_bidi_markers: true' in tokenizer kwargs and q4 output improved for that sample. BLEU delta reduced to -1.4 vs float16 for that subset.

kenji: Good. For CJK token explosion, try enabling 'mecab_pretokenize': true for ja and 'jieba_presegment': true for zh in tokenizer config. Also compare using byte-level BPE to see if merges restored.

anika: Plan: run small matrix: quant settings [q4_0, q8_0, float16], tokenizer variants [default, nfkc_normalize, jieba_preseg]. 3x3 matrix ~9 jobs. I'll kick them off on dedicated infra.

infra-bot: Scheduled 9 jobs on ded-gpu-pool-3; job IDs: 9876-9884. ETA ~50m.

liam: Nice. Also add eval metric: chrF and COMET for ar, and token_growth ratio per language so we can quantify inflation.

anika: Added to runs. If CJK token growth >1.8 we short-circuit and emit a warning in the onboarding checklist.

maya: Once we have results, let's decide whether to ship q4 for multilingual by default or keep float16 fallback for RTL languages.

anika: Thanks all. I'll paste aggregated results in this thread when done. Action items: anika run matrix; kenji validate tokenizer bundle; liam add metrics to dashboard; maya update onboarding doc about preserve_bidi. :thumbsup:
